# acquire


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Most methods here read something with
[fossick](https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick), the package that does
the fetching, and add the result with
[`Vault.add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault.add).
Each document keeps where it came from in its `meta`: the URL, when it
was fetched, and for a web search the query that found it.

*Collapse the whitespace in a scraped title and cut it to `n`

`url` reads one page and converts it to markdown. Many sites answer a
script with a challenge page, a bot wall, instead of the article. With
`auto=True`, the default, fossick then tries a heavier fetcher, then a
stealthy browser, then your logged-in Chrome. `crawl` follows links from
a start page and files each page it reaches. `web` runs a web search,
reads the top `n` results and files them, keeping the query in each
document’s meta so `sources()` can still say why a page is there;
`dropped` lists the results it could not read.

### Routing: what a target is

`grab(target)` looks at a target and calls the method that reads it:
`arxiv` for an arXiv id or link, `youtube` for a YouTube link (its
transcript and metadata), `github` for a repository, `gh_file` for one
file on GitHub, `pdf` for a PDF, `add_file` for a local file, `add_tree`
for a directory, and `url` for any other web address. It is the one call
a command line or an agent needs. A source file on GitHub is not filed
as a document: its repository is cloned and indexed with kosha as code.
`crawl=True` crawls a web target instead, and `shelf=` puts the result
on a named shelf instead of the one its kind is routed to.

    **kw

*Read an arXiv paper, its metadata and full text, into the vault as kind
`arxiv`, on the `papers` shelf.*

A directory usually holds two kinds of file. Prose, such as Markdown,
notebooks and PDFs, goes into the vault with `add_dir`. Source code goes
to [kosha](03_code.ipynb), a separate index built for code, with
`index_code`. `add_tree` does both, and `grab` on a directory calls it.
If kosha fails, the source files are reported and left out rather than
filed as prose. `connect=True` runs `connect` once at the end.

A long ingest can be stopped. `add_tree`, `add_dir` and `add_files` take
`stop`, a function asked before each batch of `batch` files (50), before
each file within a batch, and before kosha, and `progress`, called as
`progress(done, total, batch)` after each batch. When `stop()` returns
True, the files already filed stay in the vault, and the result has
`cancelled` set and `unread` listing the files it did not reach. Nothing
is raised. `github` asks `stop` before the clone and then passes both to
`add_tree`. `url`, `arxiv`, `youtube`, `pdf`, `gh_file` and `add_file`
ask it before the fetch or read, and `crawl` and `web` ask it between
the pages they file, so `grab` takes `stop` and `progress` whatever the
target. A fetch already under way finishes. Without `stop` the results
are what they were before.

### Fanning an ingest out

A large tree can take hours, and a crash should not mean starting again.
`add_tree(..., queue=True)` puts the work on the vault’s job queue (see
[jobs](11_jobs.ipynb)) instead of doing it: one job per `batch` files
(50), one for the code, and with `connect=True` one more that waits
until every ingest job has run. Nothing happens until something runs the
queue, such as `poll` or `vault.q.drain()`. A crash then costs only the
batch in flight, and `jobs(kind='ingest')` shows what is left. Running a
batch twice does no harm, because the vault skips a file it already
holds, so a retried batch does only what it missed. Queueing the same
batch again while it still waits adds nothing.

### Harvest: read a page’s API, not its HTML

Many sites, shops in particular, fill a page with data from a JSON API
that the page calls in the background. Reading that API gives clean
records instead of scraped HTML. `apis(url)` loads the page, captures
the JSON calls it makes, and lists them with how many records each one
holds. `harvest(url)` picks the call with the most records, or the one
you name with `capture=`, replays it, follows its pagination when
`pages` is more than 1, and files the records as one document of kind
`data` with one section per record, so each record can be found on its
own. `add_records` files a list of dicts you already have, from any API
or export, the same way.

### Watches

A watch repeats an acquisition on a schedule: re-read a page, re-run a
web search, re-harvest an API, re-read an arXiv paper or a video,
re-`grab` a path, look for changes in a folder, or write you a reminder.
`watch(target, action=..., every='6h')` registers one. `every` takes an
interval such as `'30m'`, `'1d'` or `'1w'`, and `cron=` takes a
five-field cron expression instead. The actions are listed in `ACTIONS`,
and `kind=` is another name for `action`. Other keyword arguments go to
the action, such as `n=5` for a web search.

The clock is [pobblebonk](https://vedicreader.github.io/pobblebonk/),
which keeps its schedules in the vault file. `poll()` is the tick to
call from cron, a scheduler or an app’s timer. Each call returns jobs
whose worker died to the queue, queues a job for every watch that is
due, runs the queue, runs `connect` when any job succeeded, and every
ten minutes runs `housekeep`. A failed fetch, or one that hit a bot
wall, is retried after a growing delay, and after five attempts the job
is dead: `jobs(state='dead')` lists those and `retry_job` puts one back.
A worker killed in the middle of a fetch loses its claim on the job, its
lease, but the job itself goes back on the queue.

The next run is counted from when the last one was due, so a slow fetch
does not push later runs back. After a gap, such as a laptop asleep for
ten hours under an hourly watch, `catchup` (1 by default) says how many
of the missed runs to make up, and the rest are counted in `missed`.
`run_watch` fires one watch now, outside the queue. `pause` and
`unwatch` stop a watch; the documents it already filed stay.

A `folder` watch takes a snapshot of the files under a folder, or of
those matching `pattern`, and fires with what was added, changed or
removed since its last look. It must have `instructions`, the standing
brief for whoever reviews the change, and they come back with every
change. A `remind` watch writes or updates one note instead of fetching
anything.

`housekeep` marks a document stale when its source has moved on: a local
file deleted or changed since it was filed, or a web page (after 30
days), video (90 days) or data harvest (7 days) that no watch refreshes.
Where a watch has filed several copies of one source, the older ones are
marked superseded, and only documents that are both stale and superseded
are deleted.

def watch(
    target:str, # URL, query, arXiv id, or the text of a reminder

    cron:str=None, # or a five-field cron expression, instead of an interval
    note:str=None, # why you are watching
    start:float=None, # first run time (epoch); defaults to the next boundary
    catchup:int=1, # missed intervals to make up after a gap; the rest count as `missed`
    kind:str=None, # alias for action; what the target set calls it
    instructions:str='', # the standing brief a folder watch's reviewer gets, verbatim
    pattern:str='', # globs limiting a folder watch
    **params
)->dict: # forwarded to the action (n=, pages=, sel=, ...)
```

*Register a recurring job: re-read a page, re-run a search, re-harvest
an API, watch a folder, or remind you.*

### Images

A photo has no text to search, so the vault files what the image file
says about itself: its size, the camera, and when and where it was taken
(from its EXIF data), with any caption or labels you add. `labels=`
carries what an image classifier saw, so a picture of a galah can be
found by searching for “galah”. The pixels stay on disk, and the
document’s `path` points at them. `add_image` files one picture as kind
`image`, `add_images` files a folder, `images` lists them, and
`tag_image` adds labels or a caption later and rebuilds the searchable
text.

```

*File one picture in the vault as `kind="image"`: its metadata is the
text, the pixels stay on disk.*

`label_images` runs [anya](https://github.com/vedicreader/anya), an
image classifier, over a folder and files every picture with the labels
it found, so the pictures can be searched by what is in them. It needs
anya installed.

``` python
_m,_g = exif_meta(wren_path), exif_meta(galah_path)
_md, _gmd=image_md(_m, 'Superb-fairy-wren.-008', labels=['Superb Fairywren']), image_md(_g, 'galah', labels=['galah'])
assert 'width: 460' in _md
assert 'Superb Fairywren' in _md
```

``` python
_v = Vault(':memory:')
_r = _v.add_image(wren_path, labels=['Superb Fairywren', 'Malurus cyaneus'])
test_eq(_v.stats()['by_kind']['image'], 1)
test_eq(_v.doc(str(wren_path.resolve()))['meta']['labels'][0], 'Superb Fairywren')
assert first(_v.search('Superb Fairywren', kind='image')), 'labels have to be searchable'
test_eq(len(_v.add_images(Path.cwd(), force=True)), 2)
test_eq(len(_v.images()), 2)
# what a later model run adds is merged in, and the text is rebuilt so it is searchable too
_ = _v.tag_image(str(galah_path.resolve()), labels=['Galah'], caption='pink and grey')
test_eq(_v.doc(str(galah_path.resolve()))['meta']['labels'], ['Galah'])
assert first(_v.search('pink and grey', kind='image'))
```

``` python
import os
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
```

``` python
# fossick's json_records walk; harvest pagination uses the same
_pay = {'data': {'items': [{'a': 1}, {'a': 2}, {'a': 3}]}}
test_eq(len(json_records(_pay)), 3)
test_eq(json_records(_pay, with_key=True)[1], 'items')
test_eq(secs('6h'), 21600); test_eq(secs('1w'), 604800); test_eq(secs(90), 90)
test_eq(secs('30m'), 1800); test_eq(secs('2 days'), 172800); test_eq(secs('45s'), 45)
test_eq(secs('1h30m'), 5400); test_eq(secs('90'), 90)
test_fail(lambda: secs('whenever'), contains='not a duration')
w = v.watch('late chunking', action='web', every='1d', n=3)
test_eq(w['params'], dict(n=3))
test_eq(len(v.watches(due_only=True)), 1)
v.unwatch(w['id'])
test_eq(len(v.watches()), 0)

# a folder watch snapshots what is there and fires only on what moved; `kind` is `action` by another name
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(':memory:', offline=True)
    (Path(d)/'a.py').write_text('a = 1')
    test_fail(lambda: v.watch(d, kind='folder', every='5m'), contains='instructions')
    w = v.watch(Path(d), kind='folder', every='5m', instructions='flag any print()', pattern='*.py')   # a Path target is filed as text
    test_eq((w['kind'], w['action'], w['instructions'], w['pattern']), ('folder', 'folder', 'flag any print()', '*.py'))
    test_eq(list(w['params']['snap']), [str(Path(d)/'a.py')])
    test_eq(v.watches()[0]['kind'], 'folder'); test_eq(v.watches()[0]['pattern'], '*.py')
    test_eq(v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])['status'], 'skipped')                          # nothing moved
    (Path(d)/'b.py').write_text('print(2)'); (Path(d)/'a.py').write_text('a = 2'); os.utime(Path(d)/'a.py', (time.time()+1,)*2)
    (Path(d)/'c.txt').write_text('ignored')
    r = v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])
    test_eq((r['status'], sorted(Path(p).name for p in r['result']['added']), [Path(p).name for p in r['result']['changed']]), ('ok', ['b.py'], ['a.py']))
    test_eq(r['result']['instructions'], 'flag any print()')
    test_eq(v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])['status'], 'skipped')                          # snapshot advanced
    os.utime(Path(d)/'a.py', (time.time()-100,)*2)                                      # an older file checked out is a change too
    test_eq([Path(p).name for p in v.run_watch(v.watches()[0])['result']['changed']], ['a.py'])
    u = v.watch('https://x.test', action='url', every='1d')                             # old spelling still works
    test_eq((u['kind'], u['instructions'], u['pattern']), ('url', '', ''))
    # a row written before the columns existed reads back with defaults
    v.db.q("update watches set instructions=NULL, pattern=NULL where id=?", [u['id']])
    test_eq((v._watch_row(u['id'])['instructions'], v._watch_row(u['id'])['pattern']), ('', ''))
    # `pattern` is a column now, and a harvest still receives it
    _got = {}
    v.harvest = lambda t, **kw: (_got.update(kw), dict(pages=1))[1]
    h = v.watch('https://x.test/shop', action='harvest', every='1d', pattern='*/api/*', pages=2)
    test_eq((h['pattern'], h['params']), ('*/api/*', dict(pages=2)))
    test_eq(v.run_watch(v._watch_row(h['id']))['status'], 'ok')
    test_eq((_got['pattern'], _got['pages']), ('*/api/*', 2))
```
